functions.name: decideFloodMap
functions.input: point feature count, the lot's plan names, and the set of plans that publish a flood map
functions.output: floodProne true, false or null plus the plain sentence for the page
functions.if_none: a null count or a null plan set both return floodProne null, never false

values.if_missing: shown as Not known — no published flood map

break_it.scenario: the lot is outside the 10 councils that publish a flood planning map
break_it.what_happens: the page would say Flood: No when nobody checked the land at all
break_it.how: decideFloodMap returns null unless the lot's plan publishes a map

break_it.scenario: the ArcGIS layer returns HTTP 200 with an error body
break_it.what_happens: an error would be read as no polygon here and shown as No

break_it.scenario: the distinct-plans request fails on a cold server
break_it.what_happens: every lot would be shown not known until the list loads
break_it.how: a failure is not cached, the next request retries
break_it.repro: block mapprod3 once, then load two addresses

break_it.scenario: pattern book eligibility receives null flood
break_it.what_happens: an unknown flood status is not listed as a potential exclusion
break_it.how: unchanged from before (it was always false); logged for the pattern-book step

break_it.scenario: extra latency from two more map calls on every page load
break_it.what_happens: the property lookup could take longer for the reader
break_it.how: point query is one call; plan list cached per server instance

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes — a Hornsby flood lot shows Yes; Winston Hills shows Not known — no published flood map
